display.purpose: Copperplate engraved caps — artist name, section plates, category labels. Always uppercase, tracked.

body.purpose: Cormorant weight 300 — bios, project descriptions, statements. Held at ~60ch.

label.purpose: futura-pt geometric caps — descriptors, scroll cue, micro-labels. Tracking ≥0.30em.

motion.name: ease-signature
motion.purpose: The single system easing (ease-out-quart family). Every transition and entrance uses it.

motion.name: pill-spring
motion.purpose: The active-pill fill sliding between category tabs (layoutId).

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Control invert-on-hover (200ms) and nav link/color-theme flips (300ms).

motion.name: section-dissolve
motion.purpose: Adjacent full-viewport sections crossfade through the graphite ground. Opacity only.

components.name: Category Pill (active)
components.description: The selected Work category tab — a single dark cell that slides between tabs.
components.css: .ds-pill-active { position: relative; border: none; border-radius: 9999px; padding: 8px 22px; background: var(--oxidized-graphite, #1A1A1C); color: var(--bone-porcelain, #F3EEE8); font-family: 'futura-pt', 'Copperplate Gothic Light', sans-serif; font-size: 9.5px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.20em; cursor: pointer; }

components.name: Category Pill (inactive)
components.description: An unselected Work category — dashed, provisional, waiting to be chosen.
components.css: .ds-pill-inactive { position: relative; border: 1px dashed rgba(26,26,28,0.40); border-radius: 9999px; padding: 8px 22px; background: rgba(243,238,232,0.50); color: var(--oxidized-graphite, #1A1A1C); font-family: 'futura-pt', 'Copperplate Gothic Light', sans-serif; font-size: 9.5px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.20em; cursor: pointer; transition: color 0.2s, border-color 0.2s; } .ds-pill-inactive:hover { border-color: rgba(26,26,28,0.7); }

components.name: Arrow Button (light theme)
components.description: Square gallery/next-project control on a light surface. Inverts fully on hover.
components.html: <button class="ds-arrow-light" aria-label="Next image"><svg width="13" height="13" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"><path d="M9 6l6 6-6 6"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-arrow-light { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 36px; height: 36px; border: 1px solid rgba(26,26,28,0.30); border-radius: 0; background: transparent; color: var(--oxidized-graphite, #1A1A1C); cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s, color 0.2s, transform 0.2s; } .ds-arrow-light:hover { background: var(--oxidized-graphite, #1A1A1C); color: var(--bone-porcelain, #F3EEE8); transform: scale(1.05); } .ds-arrow-light:active { transform: scale(0.94); }

components.name: Arrow Button (dark theme)
components.description: Same control on a dark surface — light border/glyph, inverts to a bone fill.
components.html: <button class="ds-arrow-dark" aria-label="Next image"><svg width="13" height="13" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"><path d="M9 6l6 6-6 6"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-arrow-dark { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 36px; height: 36px; border: 1px solid rgba(243,238,232,0.30); border-radius: 0; background: transparent; color: var(--bone-porcelain, #F3EEE8); cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s, color 0.2s, transform 0.2s; } .ds-arrow-dark:hover { background: var(--bone-porcelain, #F3EEE8); color: var(--oxidized-graphite, #1A1A1C); transform: scale(1.05); } .ds-arrow-dark:active { transform: scale(0.94); }

components.name: Nav Link
components.description: Floating Copperplate nav link — rests dimmed, rises to full on hover. Color auto-flips per section.
components.css: .ds-nav-link { font-family: 'Copperplate Gothic Light', 'Copperplate', Georgia, serif; font-size: 14px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.20em; color: rgba(26,26,28,0.55); text-decoration: none; transition: color 0.3s; } .ds-nav-link:hover { color: var(--oxidized-graphite, #1A1A1C); }

narrative.overview: The site is a clinical display case for a practice about the body under engineering. Work is presented as specimens — lit from the dark, held still, examined — and the interface is the vitrine: cold, exact glass that frames a charged, bodily subject without ever competing with it. The whole experience runs two registers of the same case: a dark world (the lit vitrine — oxidized-graphite ground, cinematic imagery, hairline serifs) carries atmosphere and first impression, and a light world (the catalogue card — bone-porcelain ground, dark ink, taxonomic labels) carries the index. The single fixed nav flips between them automatically, so moving through the site feels like turning a specimen from its dramatic display into its documentation and back. Density is low and deliberate; depth is soft and atmospheric, not stacked — no drop shadows, only tonal gradients, opacity dissolves, and functional text-shadow.
keyCharacteristics: Two-world system: dark cinematic vitrine ↔ light catalogue index, nav auto-flips.
Specimen-first: imagery leads, the interface recedes to glass.
Atmospheric depth, zero drop shadows — dissolves, gradients, crossfades.
Hairline, uppercase, widely-tracked typography as instrument labeling.
Refined unease by precision and low light, never by shock.

rules.name: The Two-Worlds Rule
rules.body: Every surface is either dark-world (oxidized-graphite ground, bone-porcelain type, data-nav-theme dark) or light-world (bone-porcelain ground, oxidized-graphite type, data-nav-theme light). There is no third ground; new sections declare their world and never invent a mid-gray in between.

rules.name: The One-Skin Rule
rules.body: synthetic-flesh is the only accent and it is rare — reserved for moments that reference the body (accents, hovers, the descriptor). It is prohibited as a button fill, a background, or a section device. Its scarcity is what makes it read as flesh and not as brand color.

rules.name: The Tracked-Caps Rule
rules.body: Every Copperplate and Futura label is uppercase and widely tracked (≥0.20em). Sentence-case display type is forbidden; these fonts are labels, not headlines.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Cormorant body always runs at weight 300, never bolder. The thin literary line is the reading voice of the whole system; a heavier body weight reads as a different, wrong site.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Drop shadows are prohibited. If an element needs separation, use a tonal gradient, an opacity dissolve, or the wet-petroleum surface step. A box-shadow anywhere in this system is a bug.

rules.name: The Functional-Glow Rule
rules.body: text-shadow exists to keep light type readable over dark imagery and nothing else. It is never applied to type on a solid surface for effect.

dos: Do anchor every surface to one of the two worlds (dark #1A1A1C ground / #F3EEE8 type, or light #F3EEE8 ground / #1A1A1C type) and declare its data-nav-theme.
Do let imagery lead — the specimen holds the room; type, spacing, and motion frame it.
Do keep all display/label type uppercase and tracked ≥0.20em (Copperplate) and body type Cormorant weight 300.
Do convey depth with tonal gradients, opacity dissolves, and the wet-petroleum step — atmospheric, not stacked.
Do reserve synthetic-flesh (#C9A48F) for rare, body-referencing accents and hovers only.
Do hold body measure at ~60ch and keep the cinematic motion behind a prefers-reduced-motion crossfade fallback.
donts: Don't ship a generic Squarespace/template portfolio — a white grid of equal thumbnails with a neutral sans and no point of view.
Don't apply startup/SaaS polish: no bright/rounded/gradient-accent styling, no hero-metric blocks, no product-landing cadence.
Don't drift into gothic/horror kitsch — no skulls, gore, blood-drip, or Halloween darkness. The unease is clinical and refined.
Don't go busy or maximalist: no clutter, no loud stacking, no animation for its own sake competing with the work.
Don't add a box-shadow anywhere — a drop shadow in this system is a bug.
Don't use synthetic-flesh as a button fill, background, or section device; don't invent a third mid-gray ground; don't set body type above weight 300.
